listitem.para: a == b on two NetObjects is true when they stand for the same .NET object, however each came to Rexx.

A .NET object that goes to Rexx and back is the object itself; a Rexx object that goes to .NET and back is the object itself, also the instance of a Rexx class that extends a .NET class, with its class and its state.

A NetObject keeps its .NET object alive while Rexx holds it; a RexxObject keeps its Rexx object alive while .NET holds it. The instances of Rexx classes that extend .NET classes, and the handlers .NET can call, are released by the two garbage collectors, with nothing to do by hand.
A name, once found to be a namespace or a type, stays that namespace or type; a member is looked up when the message arrives.

An exception thrown by .NET is in condition("O")~additional[2], and is the InnerException of the RexxException if it goes back to .NET; a Rexx condition that goes through .NET and back is raised again as it was.
No call into ooRexx is made from .NET's finalizer thread, and none with a lock of the bridge held: uninit methods run on Rexx threads.
A thread waiting in .NET (.net~nextEvent, a long .NET call) holds no interpreter lock: other Rexx threads run, and .NET can call Rexx back on any thread meanwhile.
One binary of the bridge works with every .NET from 8 on, and the same net.cls on the three systems.
